architecture_decisions.title: PostgreSQL as primary database
architecture_decisions.context: Loyalty program requires ACID transactions for points ledger (strong consistency per NFR-08). Need pgvector extension for future personalisation.
architecture_decisions.decision: Use PostgreSQL as the single relational database for all loyalty services in Sprint 1. Points ledger requires row-level locking for concurrent redemption safety.
architecture_decisions.consequences: Strong consistency guaranteed. Horizontal read scaling via read replicas. Must manage connection pooling (PgBouncer). Schema migrations via versioned migration tool.

architecture_decisions.title: JWT + Refresh Token for customer authentication
architecture_decisions.context: Customers access via mobile app (long sessions) and web (shorter sessions). Need stateless auth for horizontal scaling.
architecture_decisions.decision: Short-lived JWT access tokens (15 min) + long-lived refresh tokens (30 days mobile, 7 days web). Refresh tokens stored in DB for revocation capability.
architecture_decisions.consequences: Stateless verification for most requests (no DB hit). Revocation requires checking refresh token on renewal. Token rotation on each refresh prevents replay.

architecture_decisions.title: Event-driven notification delivery
architecture_decisions.context: Multiple features trigger notifications (points earned, redeemed, expired, tier change). Notification delivery must not block business logic.
architecture_decisions.decision: Business services emit domain events (e.g., points.earned). Notification service consumes events asynchronously, renders templates, dispatches via appropriate channel.
architecture_decisions.consequences: Decoupled: business logic unaffected by notification failures. Retry with backoff on delivery failure. Dead letter queue for undeliverable notifications.

architecture_decisions.title: Monorepo with service-per-bounded-context
architecture_decisions.context: Sprint 1 establishes foundation. Team is small. Need fast iteration without premature distribution complexity.
architecture_decisions.decision: Monorepo with clear module boundaries: auth-service, notification-service, loyalty-core (Sprint 2+). Deploy as separate containers from same repo. Shared libraries for common concerns (logging, auth middleware, error handling).
architecture_decisions.consequences: Fast development, shared tooling, atomic commits across services. Must enforce module boundaries via linting. Can extract to separate repos later if team grows.

architecture_decisions.title: Redis for session cache and rate limiting
architecture_decisions.context: Rate limiting (registration, OTP, login) needs shared state across service instances. Balance cache (Sprint 2) needs sub-500ms reads.
architecture_decisions.decision: Redis cluster for: rate limit counters (sliding window), session metadata, and future points balance cache. TTL-based expiry for all keys.
architecture_decisions.consequences: Fast reads for rate limiting without DB load. Must handle Redis unavailability gracefully (fail-open for reads, fail-closed for writes). Cluster mode for HA.

architecture_decisions.title: Kafka for domain events
architecture_decisions.context: Need reliable event delivery for notifications, future analytics, and cross-service communication. Must guarantee at-least-once delivery.
architecture_decisions.decision: Kafka (or managed equivalent: MSK/Confluent/Event Hubs) for all domain events. Topics: customer.registered, notification.send, points.earned (Sprint 2+). Consumer groups per service.
architecture_decisions.consequences: Durable event log enables replay. Partition by customer_id for ordering. Must handle idempotent consumers (deduplication). Schema registry for contract evolution.

architecture_decisions.title: Cross-platform mobile with React Native
architecture_decisions.context: Need iOS + Android app. Small team. Design system must be shared. Barcode scanning and push notifications required.
architecture_decisions.decision: React Native for mobile app. Shared component library between web (React) and mobile (React Native) where possible. Native modules for push tokens and biometric auth.
architecture_decisions.consequences: Single codebase for both platforms. Faster iteration. Some native bridge work for push/biometric. Performance acceptable for loyalty app (not gaming/video).

risks.risk: Email deliverability for OTP — emails may land in spam
risks.mitigation: Use dedicated transactional email domain with SPF/DKIM/DMARC. Monitor delivery rates. Provide 'resend' with clear instructions to check spam.

risks.risk: Social login provider outage blocks registration/login
risks.mitigation: Social login is optional — email/password always available as fallback. Circuit breaker on social provider calls (3 failures → 30s break).

risks.risk: Rate limiting too aggressive blocks legitimate users
risks.mitigation: Start with generous limits (5 registrations/IP/hour, 3 OTPs/10min). Monitor false positive rate. Make limits configurable without code deploy.

risks.risk: Push token registration fails silently on some Android devices
risks.mitigation: Retry token registration on app foreground. Fall back to email for notifications if no valid push token.

risks.risk: Database schema changes in Sprint 2 require migration of Sprint 1 data
risks.mitigation: Design tables with nullable columns for future fields. Use versioned migrations. All Sprint 1 tables designed with Sprint 2-4 needs in mind.

dependency_order: US-001 (Infrastructure) must complete first — all other stories depend on cluster + DB
US-008 (CI/CD) should complete early Sprint 1 — enables automated deployment for all subsequent work
US-006 (Design System Core) and US-001 can run in parallel — no dependency
US-002 (API Gateway) depends on US-001 — needs cluster to deploy to
US-004 (Logging) depends on US-001 — needs cluster
US-009 (Notification Service) depends on US-001 — needs Kafka + email provider
US-011 (App Shell) depends on US-006 — needs design system components
US-015 (Registration) depends on US-002 (gateway) + US-006 (design system)
US-018 (OTP) depends on US-015 — needs account to verify
US-020 (Login) depends on US-018 — needs verified account
US-021 (Social Login) depends on US-020 — extends login flow
US-023 (T&C) depends on US-015 — part of registration flow
reasoning: Sprint 1 establishes the complete technical foundation and customer identity layer. Architecture decisions prioritise simplicity (monorepo, single DB) while maintaining clear boundaries for Sprint 2+ extraction. PostgreSQL chosen for ACID guarantees on the financial ledger. Event-driven notifications decouple business logic from delivery. JWT auth enables stateless horizontal scaling. All tables designed with future sprints in mind (nullable columns for tier_id, loyalty fields). The dependency order ensures infrastructure is ready before application code, and design system is ready before UI screens.
